clue.text: Shows emotion as layabout's dropping piece of litter

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go

blocks.note: a slob is a lazy layabout; the 's makes it SLOB'S, read as SLOBS
the first piece of 'litter' is its L, which is removed

explanation.surface: A slob sheds a tear as a scrap of rubbish falls from their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on 'layabout's' has to be taken as part of the word, giving SLOBS rather than SLOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sobs is showing emotion.

clue.text: Party-pooper ruins wine

blocks.note: to spoil something is to ruin it
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A killjoy wrecks the wine at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruins' looks like a noun, as in old castles, but it is the verb SPOILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport is someone who stops others enjoying themselves, a party-pooper.

clue.text: Spider letting no light through glass: number will depart

blocks.note: something black lets no light through
a window is a pane of glass
N is the standard abbreviation for number; it is removed from WINDOW

explanation.surface: A spider sits on a blacked-out pane while a figure is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass' suggests the spider is seen through a pane, but it is only there to supply the word the number leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The black widow is a well-known venomous spider.

clue.text: A road race, one through island heading west: it's within your reach

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorbike road race
one = a, as in 'a book'
a loose equivalence, as in coming in by the door; this part of the parse is uncertain
Elba, Napoleon's island of exile, reversed

explanation.surface: A motorbike race passes over an island and heads off westward.
explanation.walkthrough: A TT and reversed ELBA are secure, but 'one through' is less certain: read here as A + IN, it may be meant to work some other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what can be attained, reached or achieved, lies within your grasp.

clue.text: Pub grub done perfectly – that is, including starter of scampi

blocks.note: done 'to a T' means done perfectly; S goes in after TOA
the first letter of scampi
i.e. is Latin 'id est', that is

explanation.surface: A pub meal cooked just right, with scampi to start.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside TO A T, giving TOAST, and IE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a typical British pub snack.

clue.text: Form of Tehran A-Z that shows Nazareth?

definitions.text: Form of Tehran A-Z that shows Nazareth?

blocks.note: the surface reads this as an edition of a street atlas of Tehran; the setter means a rearranged form of the letters TEHRANAZ
the surface suggests a map marking the town; the setter means the letters rearrange to spell NAZARETH

explanation.surface: An A-to-Z street map of Tehran somehow shows the town of Nazareth.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the very device crosswords use: TEHRAN A-Z is an anagram of NAZARETH.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram is a word formed by rearranging another's letters, as these two are.

clue.text: Bigoted pastime offering nasty moment?

blocks.note: narrow-minded, bigoted
a pastime is an escape from everyday life

explanation.surface: An intolerant person's hobby turns out to be unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'nasty moment' is a loose definition: a narrow escape is a scary moment you survive.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is a close shave, a nasty moment that ends well.

clue.text: Panted audibly, being unhappy

indicators.note: tells you to go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: blew = panted, as in huffed and puffed

explanation.surface: Someone is breathing hard and feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: BLEW and BLUE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling unhappy.

clue.text: Everyman's beginning to get doddery regularly: one going round in circles

indicators.note: take letters at a fixed interval, here every third

blocks.note: first letter of Everyman
the 1st, 4th and 7th letters: D-od-D-er-Y

explanation.surface: The setter admits to becoming a bit doddery and dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' usually means every other letter, but here the step is every third letter of 'doddery'. 'To get' just links the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water or air that goes round in circles.

clue.text: Gemstone from old friend

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A precious stone handed down by a long-time friend.
explanation.walkthrough: O for old is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: opal is an iridescent stone prized in jewellery.

clue.text: Administered a sporting venue, went to seed

blocks.note: to run something is to administer it
taken as written
a football or cricket ground

explanation.surface: Someone managed a stadium that fell into neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is exact but the definition is loose: both phrases mean came to grief or failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture that ran aground came to nothing, much as something that has gone to seed has declined.

clue.text: Couple of things fiddler does to curry favour

blocks.note: a violinist bows, and a poor one scrapes
to fawn, like a servant bending low before a master

explanation.surface: A fiddler's two moves are ways of sucking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddler' suggests a cheat or swindler, but here it means a violin player.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow and scrape is to fawn on someone to win favour.

clue.text: Oriental oak represented in body of water

indicators.note: re-presented: the letters are presented again in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: An eastern oak tree is painted into a picture of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' reads as 'depicted', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Ontario, one of North America's Great Lakes, is a body of water.

clue.text: Leaders' laws announced

definitions.note: the clue's 'Leaders'' is possessive, standing for the plural noun

indicators.note: something announced is spoken, so go by sound

blocks.note: principles = laws

explanation.surface: The rulers' decrees are proclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: Either spelling could be the answer on sound alone, so the crossing letters decide: MAGI gives A in 8th place, so PRINCIPALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Principals are leaders, such as the heads of schools.

clue.text: Stitch up peripheral creatives after time in Caribbean location

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom

blocks.note: to stitch is to sew; it is reversed
T is the standard abbreviation for time
indies are independent artists and labels, working outside the mainstream

explanation.surface: Someone frames a group of fringe artists while on a Caribbean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' looks like the slang for framing someone, but it splits into stitch (SEW) and up (reverse it).
explanation.definitionFit: A geographical name: the island chain that encloses the Caribbean Sea, so a place there is a Caribbean location.

clue.text: Soldier's own

blocks.note: the lowest rank in the army
adjective: belonging to one person, not shared

explanation.surface: Something belongs to a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is not possessive: it stands for 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One word, two senses: the rank of an ordinary soldier, and the adjective for what is yours alone rather than public.

clue.text: Tennis ace in ceremony, abrupt, acting up

indicators.note: cut off short, so the last letter goes
behaving wildly, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: CEREMONY loses its last letter, Y

explanation.surface: A tennis star at a formal event is short-tempered and misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting, since John McEnroe was notorious for tantrums on court.
explanation.definitionFit: John McEnroe was a top tennis player of the 1980s.

clue.text: Make second purchase of wind instrument that's not about

blocks.note: the recorder is a simple woodwind instrument
c. (circa) = about; it is removed

explanation.surface: Someone buys another wind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'about' is circa, as in dates like c.1500.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to order again, making a second purchase.

clue.text: Stretch on the house, move unimpeded

blocks.note: a run is a stretch, as of good luck
on the house means free of charge

explanation.surface: A spell of free drinks lets everyone roam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the house' sounds like a place, but it is the phrase for something given free.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: animals let off the lead or out of a pen roam wherever they like, with nothing holding them back.

clue.text: On two occasions, firm crazy for tropical food

indicators.note: the next item is used twice

blocks.note: Co. = company, a firm
used a second time
a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A company repeatedly goes wild for exotic food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On two occasions' tells you to take CO twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the nut of the palm that grows on tropical beaches.

clue.text: In décor, one tends to show flashy item

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: déCOR ONE Tends

explanation.surface: An interior designer's choices reveal a showy ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the accent and the comma: the letters run straight across.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown, a showy piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Device shrinking, about to become quiet

blocks.note: a contraction is a shrinking
c. (circa) = about; this C is swapped out
p (piano) = quiet in music; it replaces the C

explanation.surface: A gadget shrinks until it is almost silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The second C of CONTRACTION turns into P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though the answer usually carries a hint of something odd or improvised.

clue.text: Symbol of love seen in bedrooms, on-and-off

indicators.note: take a letter, skip a letter

blocks.note: b-E-d-R-o-O-m-S, the even letters

explanation.surface: A token of love appears in bedrooms now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer, since bedrooms are where Eros is most at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, and his statue in London's Piccadilly Circus is a famous symbol of it.

clue.text: A small island with a vast stretch of land

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
I is the standard abbreviation for island
'with' adds the second A

explanation.surface: A little island comes with a huge expanse of land.
explanation.walkthrough: The contrast between a small island and a vast continent is the joke of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the largest continent is literally a vast stretch of land.

clue.text: Arrest aunt misbehaving in eatery

indicators.note: the letters are out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: Police detain an unruly aunt at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The unruly aunt paints a scene, but 'misbehaving' just shuffles the ten letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an eatery is informal for any place that serves meals.

clue.text: Primarily, men attending godliest infant?

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: Men Attending Godliest Infant

explanation.surface: Wise men visit the holiest of babies.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the Magi were the men who came to the infant Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi are the three wise men who visited the newborn Jesus.

clue.text: In biblical books, Lawrence is moved to find assertions of facts

blocks.note: the Old and New Testaments
T.E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia'; TE moves from the front to after STA

explanation.surface: Lawrence is shifted about inside the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: T.E. Lawrence is 'Lawrence of Arabia', the British officer and author, and his initials happen to open the word for the Bible's two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a statement is a formal declaration of what is so.

clue.text: Pass out, seeing venomous menaces

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters

explanation.surface: Someone faints at the sight of snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' reads as one phrase meaning faint, but it splits into the fodder and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the asp is an Egyptian cobra, famous as Cleopatra's means of suicide.
